questions.question: A sales manager's spreadsheet lists each salesperson's monthly sales in cells B2 through B9. Which formula would calculate the total sales for all salespeople?
questions.explanation: =SUM(B2:B9). The SUM function adds all values in a range, so it gives the total sales. AVERAGE would divide the total by the number of salespeople, giving average sales per person. COUNT returns how many cells contain numbers, which here is eight. MAX returns the single highest value, showing the top salesperson's result rather than the team total.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic spreadsheet applications

questions.question: Software that lets employees in different locations edit the same document at the same time supports knowledge management by enabling
questions.explanation: Collaboration. Real-time co-editing tools help people combine what they know and build on each other's ideas without being in the same room, which is collaboration. Encryption protects data from being read by outsiders, backups protect against data loss, and automation uses technology to perform tasks without human effort, but none of these is the main benefit of shared editing.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of technology in knowledge management

questions.question: Achieving goals by planning, organizing, directing, and controlling resources is
questions.explanation: Management. Management coordinates people and resources to accomplish an organization's goals through its core functions. Production creates goods and services, finance manages money, and marketing connects products with customers. Managers work in all of these areas.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of management

questions.question: Organizations that encourage employees to keep learning tend to
questions.explanation: Adapt to change more easily. When employees continually build new skills and knowledge, they are more comfortable with new ideas and better prepared to adjust when conditions change. Learning supports innovation rather than discouraging it, and it doesn't directly determine how many managers an organization needs.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe relationship among innovation, learning, and change

questions.question: When employees first learn about a major change at work, a common reaction is
questions.explanation: Resistance. Change often creates uncertainty about how jobs and routines will be affected, so resistance and anxiety are normal early reactions. With communication and support, people usually move toward acceptance and commitment. Immediate commitment and celebration are uncommon first responses, and complete indifference is less typical than concern.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the change-management lifecycle

questions.question: How can an efficient supply chain give a business a competitive advantage?

options.A: By limiting the number of customers the business serves
options.B: By allowing the business to raise prices on every product
options.C: By lowering costs and speeding delivery
options.D: By letting the business use lower-quality materials

questions.explanation: By lowering costs and speeding delivery. Efficient supply chains reduce waste, inventory costs, and delays, allowing a business to offer lower prices, faster delivery, or better availability than competitors. Raising prices, cutting quality, or limiting customers would weaken rather than strengthen its competitive position.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the impact of supply chain on business performance

questions.question: A fake email designed to trick employees into revealing passwords is
questions.explanation: Phishing. Phishing messages pretend to come from trusted sources, such as a bank or the company's IT department, to steal login information or install malware. Spam filters, encryption, and firewalls are defenses that help protect against threats like phishing. Training employees to recognize and report suspicious messages is one of the most effective ways to protect a business's digital assets.

performanceIndicator.text: Comply with strategies for protecting business' digital assets (e.g., website, social media, email, etc.)

questions.question: At Brightline Engineering, senior designers keep their best calculation shortcuts to themselves because they believe the knowledge makes them harder to replace. Management worries this slows down newer engineers and creates risk if a senior designer leaves. Which knowledge-management issue is the company facing?
questions.explanation: Knowledge hoarding. Knowledge hoarding occurs when employees withhold useful knowledge for personal advantage, such as job security. It hurts the organization by slowing others and creating gaps when the hoarder leaves. Knowledge piracy involves stealing knowledge, data mining is analyzing large data sets for patterns, and redundancy means storing the same information in several places.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of ethics in knowledge management

questions.question: Northgate Utilities expects 30% of its senior engineers to retire within five years. Leaders worry that decades of experience with the company's aging equipment will be lost. Which of the following would best capture that knowledge before the engineers leave:

options.A: Hiring a consultant to rewrite the company's job descriptions
options.B: Raising senior engineers' salaries to delay their retirement
options.C: Having engineers record key repairs and mentor junior staff
options.D: Buying newer equipment that requires less frequent repair

questions.explanation: Having engineers record key repairs and mentor junior staff. Recorded walk-throughs capture explicit steps, and pairing junior staff with experts transfers the experience-based judgment that is hard to write down. Higher salaries might delay some retirements but don't capture the knowledge before engineers eventually leave. Rewriting job descriptions doesn't preserve technical know-how, and newer equipment still needs to be repaired by people who understand it.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify techniques that can be used to capture and transfer knowledge in an organization

questions.question: After a project ends, a team stores its templates and lessons learned in a shared library. Which knowledge-management process is the team completing:
questions.explanation: Storing knowledge for future use. Storing knowledge where others can find it lets future teams reuse what worked and avoid repeating mistakes. Sales forecasts, recruiting, and performance reviews are other business processes that don't involve capturing and storing knowledge.

performanceIndicator.text: Apply knowledge management processes

questions.question: Which of the following questions is most important when evaluating an online source for a business report:

options.A: Who published it, and what evidence supports it?
options.B: How many advertisements appear alongside the article?
options.C: How long is the article compared with similar articles?
options.D: How many images and graphics does the page contain?

questions.explanation: Who published it, and what evidence supports it? A source's reliability depends on who created it, their expertise and possible bias, and whether claims are backed by evidence. The number of images or ads and the length of an article say little about accuracy. Checking the publication date is also important, since outdated information can lead to poor decisions.

performanceIndicator.text: Evaluate quality and source of information

questions.question: A customer claims a store's faulty ladder caused her injury and takes the store to court to recover her medical costs. In this case, the customer is the
questions.explanation: Plaintiff. The plaintiff brings the lawsuit and claims to have been harmed. The defendant is the party being sued, an appellant is a party who asks a higher court to review a decision, and a mediator is a neutral third party who helps people settle disputes outside of court. Knowing these roles helps business owners understand what happens when legal action is taken against them or by them.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the litigation process

questions.question: Which of the following should a business do to make its web pages more accessible to people who use screen readers:

options.B: Add descriptive alt text to images
options.C: Use images of text instead of real text
options.D: Use only color to show important information

questions.explanation: Add descriptive alt text to images. Alt text describes images so screen readers can tell users what they show. Images of text can't be read by screen readers, headings help users navigate, and relying only on color excludes users who can't distinguish colors.

performanceIndicator.text: Create and post basic web page

questions.question: The risk that changes in currency values will reduce a company's international profits is
questions.explanation: Exchange-rate risk. When a company sells in another country, the money it earns must be converted back to its home currency, and changes in exchange rates can reduce that value. Product-liability risk involves harm caused by products, natural risk comes from weather and disasters, and credit risk is the chance a borrower won't repay.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe international considerations affecting risk management

questions.question: A restaurant manager is short two servers for the summer season. Which of the following would be the most appropriate first step in filling the positions:

options.A: Posting an ad without describing the jobs
options.B: Identifying the skills and availability the jobs require
options.C: Offering the jobs to the first two people who apply
options.D: Asking current servers to work double shifts all summer

questions.explanation: Identifying the skills and availability the jobs require. Before recruiting, a manager should define what the job requires, including skills, hours, and duties, so the right candidates are attracted and chosen. Hiring the first applicants risks a poor fit, constant double shifts can burn out current staff, and a vague ad attracts unqualified applicants and wastes time for everyone.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe managerial considerations in staffing

questions.question: Pairing a new employee with an experienced worker to learn on the job is
questions.explanation: Mentoring. Mentoring transfers knowledge, especially hard-to-document know-how, through ongoing guidance from someone experienced. Outsourcing hires another company to perform work, benchmarking compares practices with those of leading organizations, and downsizing reduces the number of employees.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify techniques that can be used to capture and transfer knowledge in an organization

questions.question: A store manager must decide whether to add a weekend delivery service. Which of the following pieces of information would be most useful for this decision:

options.A: The store's sales of its best-selling product
options.B: The number of years the store has been open
options.C: The delivery service offered by a store in another state
options.D: Customer demand and the cost of the service

questions.explanation: Customer demand and the cost of the service. Customer demand and costs show whether a weekend service would be used and whether it would be profitable, which directly supports the decision. Sales of one best-selling product don't show whether customers want weekend delivery. How long the store has been open doesn't predict demand, and a store in another state serves different customers. Assessing information needs means focusing on information that affects the decision.

performanceIndicator.text: Assess information needs

questions.question: A customer tells a salon receptionist that her phone number has changed. Which of the following is the best response:

options.A: Tell her to update it online herself later
options.B: Write the new number on a sticky note
options.C: Leave the old number since it might still work
options.D: Update her record right away and confirm the new number

questions.explanation: Update her record right away and confirm the new number. Updating the record immediately and confirming the number prevents errors and ensures the salon can reach her about appointments. Sticky notes are easily lost, asking her to do it later risks it never happening, and keeping an outdated number means reminders and messages won't reach her.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain customer records

questions.question: A project to open a new store is three weeks behind schedule. The project manager adds two more contractors to finish the tasks on the critical path more quickly, increasing the cost. This schedule-compression technique is called
questions.explanation: Crashing. Crashing adds resources to critical tasks to shorten the schedule, usually at extra cost. Fast tracking overlaps tasks that were planned in sequence, scope reduction removes work from the project, and baselining saves the approved plan for later comparison.

performanceIndicator.text: Manage project schedule

questions.question: Depending on a single overseas supplier for a critical part increases a company's exposure to
questions.explanation: Supply chain disruptions. When a company relies on one distant supplier, a single event such as a port closure, natural disaster, or political conflict can stop deliveries and halt production. Zoning laws, employee turnover, and seasonal swings in demand are risks too, but they aren't caused by relying on one overseas supplier.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss global supply chain issues

questions.question: Requiring employees to wear name badges and sign in visitors at the front desk is an example of a(n)
questions.explanation: Routine security precaution. Routine security precautions are everyday procedures that help protect people, property, and information, and controlling who enters a building is one of the most common. Badges make it easy to spot unauthorized people, and sign-in sheets record who is on the premises. A marketing strategy targets customers, quality-control checks inspect products or services for defects, and inventory management tracks stock levels, so none of them describe controlling building access.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain routine security precautions

questions.question: An online furniture retailer ships every order from a single warehouse in Ohio, and customers on the West Coast complain about week-long delivery times. Adding a second distribution center in Nevada would most likely

options.A: reduce the number of products offered.
options.D: shorten delivery times for western customers.

questions.explanation: Shorten delivery times for western customers. Placing inventory closer to customers shortens transit time and can lower shipping costs, which improves service in that region. A second center reduces shipping distances rather than increasing them, the retailer still needs suppliers, and the change affects where products are stored, not how many are offered.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe supply chain networks

questions.question: A business that pays its suppliers on time, communicates its needs early, and treats them fairly is most likely to receive
questions.explanation: Priority service during shortages. Suppliers, like any business, value reliable customers who are easy to work with. When supply is tight, they often give priority to those customers, along with better terms and support. Higher prices, fewer choices, and less favorable credit terms are more likely outcomes for customers who pay late or treat suppliers poorly.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain vendor/supplier relationships

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a business record:

options.B: A news article about the industry

questions.explanation: A sales invoice. Business records document a business's own transactions and activities, such as invoices, receipts, payroll records, and contracts. A competitor's ad, an industry news article, and a supplier's catalog are outside information the business may use, but they don't record its own transactions.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of business records

questions.question: Why is it important to coordinate your work with that of your team members?

options.A: To reduce communication with the team
options.B: To make individual performance impossible to measure
options.C: To complete only the tasks you enjoy
options.D: To avoid duplicated effort and missed tasks

questions.explanation: To avoid duplicated effort and missed tasks. When team members coordinate, they know who is doing what, so work isn't repeated and nothing falls through the cracks. Coordination requires more communication, not less. Choosing only enjoyable tasks puts personal preference ahead of team needs, and coordination doesn't prevent measuring each person's contribution.

performanceIndicator.text: Coordinate work with that of team members

questions.question: Which of the following is a routine security precaution a retail employee should follow when closing the store for the night:

options.A: Leave the back door propped open for the morning delivery
options.B: Count the cash drawer in view of the front window
options.C: Check that all doors and windows are locked and the alarm is set
options.D: Share the alarm code with a regular customer who offers to help

questions.explanation: Check that all doors and windows are locked and the alarm is set. Locking every entrance and arming the alarm are basic closing steps that reduce the risk of burglary and protect merchandise and employees. Propping a door open gives anyone easy access to the building overnight. Counting cash where people outside can see it invites robbery, so it should be done in a secure office. Alarm codes should only be shared with authorized employees, never with customers, however trustworthy they seem.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain routine security precautions

questions.question: Checking supplies before they are used in production to prevent problems is an example of
questions.explanation: Feedforward control. Feedforward control prevents problems before work begins, for example by inspecting raw materials as they arrive. Concurrent control monitors work while it is happening, feedback control reviews results after work is complete, and budget control focuses on spending compared with planned amounts.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of managerial control (control process, types of control, what is controlled)

questions.question: Which of the following is a common reason organizational changes fail:

options.A: The change is planned too carefully
options.B: Employees don't understand why it's needed
options.C: Leaders explain the change too clearly
options.D: Employees receive too much training on it

questions.explanation: Employees don't understand why it's needed. When people don't understand the reasons for a change, they are more likely to resist it or keep using old methods. Clear communication, training, and careful planning help changes succeed rather than causing them to fail.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of change management

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of a well-planned orientation program for new employees:

options.A: New hires become productive more quickly
options.B: It guarantees that new employees will never leave
options.C: It replaces the need for performance reviews
options.D: It eliminates the need for any later job training

questions.explanation: New hires become productive more quickly. A good orientation reduces confusion and anxiety, connects new hires with coworkers, and explains expectations, which speeds up how quickly they contribute. Orientation introduces the job but doesn't replace training for specific skills, it can improve retention but can't guarantee it, and it isn't a substitute for ongoing performance reviews.

performanceIndicator.text: Orient new employees

questions.question: Westbrook Logistics has high employee turnover, with many new hires leaving within three months. Exit interviews reveal that new employees feel unprepared and unsupported. Which of the following human resources activities would best address this problem:

options.A: Improving orientation and training for new hires
options.B: Hiring more employees without changing the process
options.C: Reducing benefits to lower the cost of turnover
options.D: Cutting the training budget to hire faster

questions.explanation: Improving orientation and training for new hires. New employees who feel prepared and supported are more likely to stay, so a stronger orientation and training program targets the cause revealed in the exit interviews. Cutting training would make new hires even less prepared. Hiring more people without changing the process would repeat the same problem. Reducing benefits would likely make employees even more likely to leave.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of human resources management

questions.question: Why should a business control who can access its information?

options.C: To protect confidential data from misuse
options.D: To keep employees from doing their jobs

questions.explanation: To protect confidential data from misuse. Limiting access to people who need certain information protects customer data, financial records, and trade secrets from theft or accidental misuse. Access controls should still let employees do their jobs, they don't exist to slow decisions, and they work alongside backups rather than replacing them.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of information management

questions.question: Which of the following is a risk that businesses face when operating in other countries:

options.A: Holiday sales increases in the home market
options.B: Higher demand from customers at home
options.C: Lower shipping costs within the United States
options.D: Political instability in the host country

questions.explanation: Political instability in the host country. International businesses can be affected by changes in government, civil unrest, new laws, or trade restrictions in the countries where they operate. Higher demand at home, lower domestic shipping costs, and home-market holiday sales are domestic conditions rather than international risks.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe international considerations affecting risk management

questions.question: The management function that involves setting goals and deciding how to achieve them is
questions.explanation: Planning. Planning comes first among the management functions because it establishes the goals and the actions needed to reach them. Organizing arranges people and resources to carry out the plan, directing guides and motivates employees, and controlling measures results and corrects course.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of managerial planning

questions.question: After an employee is injured at work, the business should

options.B: wait to see if the injury gets worse.
options.C: dispose of the equipment involved without review.
options.D: ask employees not to discuss it.

questions.explanation: Complete an accident report. An accident report documents what happened, who was involved, and what care was given. It's needed for workers' compensation and legal purposes and helps the business find and fix the cause so it doesn't happen again. Delaying action, keeping the incident quiet, or getting rid of equipment before it is reviewed prevents proper care and investigation and may violate safety regulations.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain procedures for handling accidents

questions.question: After mapping each step from the moment a customer places an online order to delivery, a retailer discovers that orders sit for an average of two days waiting for manager approval. This discovery is an example of process thinking helping to identify a
questions.explanation: Bottleneck. A bottleneck is a step that slows the entire process because work piles up there. Mapping the whole process made the approval delay visible. Nothing in the situation points to a market opportunity, an incorrect price, or a competitor, all of which would be found through other kinds of analysis.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss business process thinking and its impact

questions.question: A business that limits access to sensitive employee knowledge, such as salary data and medical information, is addressing the ethical knowledge-management issue of
questions.explanation: Privacy. Some knowledge a business holds is about people, and using or sharing it carelessly violates their privacy. Restricting access to those who truly need it is an ethical responsibility. Knowledge hoarding is when employees refuse to share useful knowledge, information overload is having more information than people can process, and intellectual property theft involves taking ideas or creations owned by someone else.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of ethics in knowledge management

questions.question: When a manager gives an employee the authority to make certain decisions, the manager is
questions.explanation: Delegating. Delegation means assigning authority and responsibility for tasks to employees, which frees the manager for other work and develops staff. Centralizing keeps decision making at the top, coordinating links the work of different people or units, and controlling compares performance with standards.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain managerial considerations in organizing

questions.question: Using customer information only for the purpose for which it was collected is an example of
questions.explanation: Ethical information management. Ethical information management means respecting customers' privacy and using their data only in ways they agreed to and would expect. Data mining analyzes large data sets for patterns, information overload means having too much information, and redundancy means storing the same data in multiple places.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in information management

questions.question: The physical parts of a computer system, such as the keyboard, monitor, and processor, are
questions.explanation: Hardware. Hardware includes all the physical components of a computer that can be touched. Software is the set of programs and instructions that tell the hardware what to do. Firmware updates change the built-in instructions that control devices, and cloud storage keeps data on remote servers accessed over the internet rather than on local physical parts.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss principles of computer systems

questions.question: Spreading false statements that damage a business's reputation is
questions.explanation: Defamation. Defamation is an intentional tort involving false statements that harm someone's reputation; spoken defamation is slander and written is libel. Negligence is a failure to use reasonable care, trespass is entering property without permission, and breach of contract is failing to keep a contractual promise, which isn't a tort.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the basic torts relating to business enterprises

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a business using technology to capture and share knowledge:

options.A: A help desk adds every solved problem to a searchable online database
options.B: A team posts its meeting schedule on a bulletin board
options.C: A supervisor explains a procedure verbally to one employee
options.D: A manager prints the employee handbook for new hires

questions.explanation: A help desk adds every solved problem to a searchable online database. Adding solved problems to a searchable database captures knowledge from many cases and makes it available to everyone later. Printing a handbook distributes existing information without technology for capture or search, a verbal explanation reaches only one person and isn't recorded, and a meeting schedule is simple information rather than know-how.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the use of technology in knowledge management

questions.question: Tomás supervises the eight employees who work the evening shift at a grocery store. He schedules breaks, assigns tasks, and handles customer issues as they come up. Tomás is a member of
questions.explanation: First-line management. First-line managers, also called supervisors, directly oversee frontline employees and day-to-day operations. Top managers set the overall direction of the company, middle managers implement strategy and supervise other managers, and the board of directors oversees the organization on behalf of its owners.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of management

questions.question: A common cause of business process changes is
questions.explanation: New technology. New technology often makes faster, cheaper, or more accurate ways of working possible, prompting businesses to change their processes. Other common causes include changing customer demands, new laws, and competition. Stable demand gives a business little reason to change, lower turnover means fewer disruptions rather than more, and a smaller advertising budget affects promotion rather than how work gets done.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the causes of business process changes

questions.question: Legal protection for a company's logo, brand name, or slogan is provided by a
questions.explanation: Trademark. A trademark protects words, names, symbols, and designs that identify a company's products and distinguish them from competitors'. A patent protects inventions, a warranty is a promise about product performance, and a lease is a contract to rent property. Protecting intangible assets such as trademarks helps businesses maintain their brand value.

performanceIndicator.text: Protect company information and intangibles

questions.question: Which of the following is required for a contract to be legally binding:

options.A: A written document for all agreements
options.B: Payment in cash at the time of signing
options.C: An offer and acceptance by competent parties
options.D: A notary's signature on every page

questions.explanation: An offer and acceptance by competent parties. A legally binding contract requires an offer, acceptance, consideration (something of value exchanged), competent parties, and a legal purpose. Notary signatures are required only for certain documents. Many oral contracts are enforceable, although some types must be in writing. Consideration can be money, goods, services, or a promise, so cash payment isn't required.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of legally binding contracts
